author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A federal judge in Boston has blocked a Homeland Security rule that would have changed how long certain foreign students, exchange visitors and journalists could remain in the United States, Reuters reported Monday.

The rule was due to take effect Tuesday. It would have capped F visas for international students and J visas for exchange visitors at four years, while I visas for foreign journalists would have been limited to 240 days, subject to the rule’s procedures.

U.S. District Judge F. Dennis Saylor said the department’s reasoning was insufficient and that the agency had not met its legal obligations, according to Reuters. The order prevents the limits from taking effect while the case proceeds.

The ruling has particular importance in Massachusetts, home to universities including Harvard and MIT that enroll large international communities. The judge said schools could face substantial costs and enrollment declines if students were forced to leave or repeatedly seek extensions under the policy.
dek: A federal judge in Boston temporarily blocked a Homeland Security rule that would have limited the duration of several student, exchange and journalist visas.
headline: Boston judge blocks visa-duration rule affecting foreign students and journalists
